senses.definition: To draw or pull (something) away or back from its original position or situation.
senses.example: VVhy vvithdravveſt thou thy hand, even thy right hand? pluck it out of thy boſome.

senses.definition: To take away or take back (something previously given or permitted); to remove, to retract.
senses.example: I wyl be his father, and he ſhal be my ſonne. And I wyl not withdrawe my mercy from him, as I haue withdrawen it frõ him that was before the[e]: […]

senses.definition: To cause or help (someone) to stop taking an addictive drug or substance; to dry out.
To take (one's eyes) off something; to look away.
senses.example: The lady looked up; her eyes met those of Mr. Watkins Tottle. She withdrew them in a sweet confusion, and Watkins Tottle did the same—the confusion was mutual.

senses.definition: To disregard (something) as belonging to a certain group.
senses.example: One [poem] by Hercules Rollock on the marriage of Anne of Denmark is better, and equal, a few names withdrawn, to any of the contemporaneous poetry of France.

senses.definition: To remove (a topic) from discussion or inquiry.
To stop (a course of action, proceedings, etc.)
senses.example: The question was put that "The Endeavour" be hired for the occasion; Mr. Alexander Briggs moved as an amendment, that the word "Fly" be substituted for the word "Endeavour;" but after some debate consented to withdraw his opposition.

senses.definition: To take back (a comment, something written, etc.); to recant, to retract.
To distract or divert (someone) from a course of action, a goal, etc.
senses.example: I doe not flie, but aduantagious care, / VVith-drevv me from the ods of multitude, […]

senses.definition: To extract (money) from a bank account or other financial deposit.
senses.example: VVhatever part of his ſtock a man employs as a capital, he alvvays expects is to be replaced to him vvith a profit. […] VVhenever he employs any part of it in maintaining unproductive hands of any kind, that part is, from that moment, vvithdravvn from his capital, and placed in his ſtock reſerved for immediate conſumption.

senses.definition: Chiefly followed by from: to leave a place, someone's presence, etc., to go to another room or place.
senses.example: [The] army togither with the kyng of Scottes and the other Lordes there founde, entred Scotland, and did muche hurte in the country of Galloway, deſtroying towns and all that they found abroade, but the people were fled and withdrawen out of theyr way. And when they had taken their pleaſure, the Kyng of Scottes retourned backe to Carleil.

senses.definition: Chiefly followed by from: to stop taking part in some activity; also, to remove oneself from the company of others, from publicity, etc.
senses.example: I vvill vvithdravv from your Company; retire to the Shades, and perform my Penance of a Thouſand Years.

senses.definition: To stop talking to or interacting with other people and start thinking thoughts not related to what is happening.
To stop taking an addictive drug or substance; to undergo withdrawal.
senses.example: Simon had tried to rob a bank while he was withdrawing, but he had been forced to surrender to the police after they had fired several volleys at him.

senses.definition: Of a man: to remove the penis from a partner's body orifice before ejaculation; to engage in coitus interruptus.
senses.example: Like a fool, I agreed to let him make love to me as long as he withdrew before he ejaculated and he promised he would, but then he didn't.

senses.definition: An act of drawing back or removing; a removal, a withdrawal or withdrawing.
senses.example: Indeed one of theſe VVitneſſes vvas over perſvvaded by ſome Perſons, to be out of the vvay, upon G. B.’s Trial; but he came aftervvards, vvith ſorrovv for his vvithdravv, and gave in his Teſtimony: […]

senses.definition: Synonym of withdraught (“a dismissal of a lawsuit with prejudice based on a plaintiff's withdrawal of the suit; a retraxit; also, a fine imposed on a plaintiff for such a dismissal”).
